problems: The schema records vassal and client relations in the overlord's ledger only. Others must carry: Roman Republic/Empire vassal_start kingdom-of-pontus 63 BC-62 AD; Seleucid Empire vassal_start kingdom-of-sophene c. 212-190 BCE; Parthian Empire vassal kingdom-of-sophene c. 110-95 BCE; Kingdom of Cappadocia loss/gain events against Pontus (-101..-97, -91..-85, -129); Kingdom of Armenia gain of Sophene at -95 (Cliopatria's Armenia holds the cells only from -80, leaving -94..-81 empty).

Cliopatria draws the Lycaonia block (123 cells, Konya and Isparta) as Pergamon (-188..-127), Pontus (-126..-78) and Galatia (-77..-26) in turn; no page opened supports any of the three. It also puts all of Galatia and Paphlagonia inside Pontus -126..-78.
Kingdom of Sophene: four of eleven shapes (-63..113) are marked wrong on one page's evidence; the reviewer should weigh it.

WebFetch returns a small model's answer to the prompt, not page text; quotes in the dossiers are those answers. The Mithridates VI page, the Galatia page and the Paphlagonia page were thin for the periods needed.

sources_total counts 24 distinct pages; the dossiers cite 36 in all because Galatia, Paphlagonia, Pergamon and the rebel dossier reuse pages opened for Pontus (Galatia cites 6 pages and Pontus 13 against budgets of 5 and 9, but no more pages were opened than the budgets allow per state: Pontus 9, Galatia 5, Pergamon 5, Paphlagonia 1 plus 4 reused, Sophene 5).
Event 'rename' for Galatia c. 63 (tribal Galatia becomes Deiotarus' kingdom) is a stretch of the rename type, kept at confidence 1.
Coordinates of Colophon, Leucae, Myndus, Samos, Thyatira (rebel dossier), Aegina (Pergamon) and Arsamosata/Egil (Sophene) are the researcher's geography, not a page's.
